name: markdown-link-validity
question: Do all internal markdown links in tracked documentation resolve to existing targets?

assertion.asserts: every internal markdown citation in a tracked *.md file names a real target, so a reader following it lands somewhere
assertion.measures: for each [text](dest) outside fenced code blocks and inline code spans, in every git-tracked *.md file (uldf.git.ls_files), whether the path resolved against the CITING FILE's directory exists in the WORKING TREE right now
known_gaps: working tree, not HEAD: an uncommitted deletion of a tracked target makes a correct citation look broken. Handled, not accepted: such targets are classified into the informational uncommitted_deletions bucket (via `git ls-files --deleted`) and never set the verdict red -- commit the deletion and the path leaves that set and fails for real.
resolution is citing-file-relative only: a repo-root-relative citation written without the relative prefix resolves to the wrong path and is reported broken.
existence, not correctness: a target that exists but no longer contains what the citing sentence claims passes -- this oracle cannot see content.
anchors are not verified: the #fragment is stripped before resolution, so a citation of a heading that no longer exists passes.
markdown link syntax only: bare or backticked paths in prose are never checked, and neither are non-.md files' contents.
